Case_07017/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Voriconazole was administered for 8 weeks. Aspiration of the joint was repeated after 4 weeks of therapy, and cultures were still positive for Prototheca wickerhamii. After 8 weeks, cultures of the joint fluid were sterile. The patient improved and did well.

description.short_caption: Stained preparation of joint fluid showing Prototheca wickerhamii.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a stained preparation of joint fluid with numerous round to oval structures of varying sizes. The structures have a central area and appear consistent with Prototheca species morphology. The background is a uniform yellowish color, suggesting a specific staining technique was used to highlight the organisms.
visible_findings: Round to oval structures with central areas

description.short_caption: Culture plate showing white, creamy colonies from an aspirate.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a culture plate with white, creamy colonies growing in a streaked pattern. The colonies appear dense and smooth, suggesting a fungal or yeast-like organism. The growth is uniform along the streak lines, indicating successful inoculation and incubation. The background is a clear agar medium.
